title: Recovery thresholds for hidden weighted sparse graphs (extended abstract)
pages:
Proceedings of Machine Learning Research vol 336:1–5, 2026                 39th Annual Conference on Learning Theory




             Recovery thresholds for hidden weighted sparse graphs

Zhe Hou                   HOUZHE @ SMAIL . NJU . EDU . CN    and Jingcheng Liu                LIU @ NJU . EDU . CN
Nanjing University


Editors: Steve Hanneke and Tor Lattimore


                                                        Abstract
          Recovering structural information from noisy high-dimensional data is a fundamental task in
     statistical inference. We investigate the information-theoretic recovery thresholds for a graph hidden
     in a randomly weighted complete graph. Specifically, an unknown graph H ∗ ∈ Hn is chosen
     uniformly at random, and hidden in a complete graph of n vertices through edge weights: for an
     edge e ∈ H ∗ , its weight is distributed independently according to Pn ; otherwise the edge weight is
     distributed independently according to Qn . The goal is to recover the hidden edge set from these
     noisy observations. Our primary focus on almost exact recovery, where all but a vanishing fraction of
     the edges of H ∗ must be identified. By choosing P = Bern(1), Q = Bern(q), this model captures
     the well-studied planted Erdős-Rényi recovery setting, and other weighted formulations such as
     Gaussian and Exponential distributions.
          Assuming a local Lipschitzness of the Rényi divergence between distributions Pn and Qn , and
     a mild density condition for the graphs Hn , we give a unified characterization of the information-
     theoretic limit for recovering almost all of H (also known as almost exact recovery).
          Our characterization uses the KL divergence DKL (Pn ∥Qn ) as the signal-to-noise metric. We
     show that there is a critical threshold Dc governed by the logarithm of the first moment threshold
     of Hn in the Erdős-Rényi random graph model G(n, p). For any constant η, if DKL ≥ (1 + η)Dc ,
     the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) achieves almost exact recovery; conversely if DKL ≤
     (1 − η)Dc , almost exact recovery is information-theoretically impossible. Our MLE analysis is based
     on an extension of Ding et al. (2020) ; While our lower bound involves deriving a distance-based
     Fano-type inequality based on Sibson’s α-mutual information, and it also extends to the task of
     partial recovery, in which only a constant λ-fraction of the hidden graph is required to be recovered.
     As a result, if DKL ≤ (λ − η)Dc , we also proved that the recovery of any λ-fraction must fail with
     high probability.
          Another interesting phenomenon exhibited by some of these models is the “All-or-Nothing”
     (AoN), where one can either recover almost all of the hidden graph or essentially nothing at all.
     For several natural distributional families, including certain Gaussian, Bernoulli and Exponential
     regimes, we establish an All-or-Nothing (AoN) threshold phenomenon at the exponential scale.
     For Gaussians, we obtained an AoN by lifting the sharp almost exact recovery threshold through
     the I-MMSE relation; For the others, we combine a second-moment argument inspired by planted
     subgraph recovery Mossel et al. (2023) with the second-order Rényi divergence. We also provide
     distributional examples where AoN is not universal at this level of generality, and our partial recovery
     lower bound is already the best possible. 1
